note: next_jwt (depends on next, jwt, jwt_auth_consumer) implements next's preview_url_generator plugin type with a 'jwt' plugin (@PreviewUrlGenerator id=jwt) as an alternative to the default simple_oauth. It is selected globally via next.settings.preview_url_generator = jwt (config next.preview_url_generator.configuration.jwt: secret_expiration, access_token_expiration). It also adds jwt_auth to decoupled_router/subrequests routes and claims via an event subscriber, but the JWT/preview traffic itself is external. All medium/hard eval state is grounded in LOCAL config: introspection reads the available plugin definitions / the active generator; execution switches next.settings.preview_url_generator to jwt (and its configuration), verified against the live next.settings and next.settings.manager. Baseline generator is simple_oauth (restored by cleanup).

evals.prompt: What does the next_jwt submodule add to the Next.js (next) module, and how does its access control differ from the default?
evals.expected_output: It adds a 'jwt' preview_url_generator plugin that signs Next.js preview/draft URLs with JSON Web Tokens, giving user-based access control, versus the default simple_oauth generator which is OAuth role/scope based.

evals.prompt: How do I make the next module use next_jwt's JWT-based preview URLs instead of the default? Which setting controls it?
evals.expected_output: Set next.settings.preview_url_generator to 'jwt' (e.g. drush cset next.settings preview_url_generator jwt). The preview_url_generator_configuration then holds secret_expiration and access_token_expiration (schema next.preview_url_generator.configuration.jwt).

evals.prompt: Besides adding a preview URL generator, what does next_jwt do to routes so a JWT-authenticated Next.js app can fetch data?
evals.expected_output: Its RouteSubscriber::alterRoutes() adds the jwt_auth authentication provider to the decoupled_router.path_translation and subrequests.front-controller routes (appending jwt_auth to each route's _auth option), and a JwtEventSubscriber adds claims when a token is generated.

evals.prompt: On this live site, inspect the next preview_url_generator plugins and confirm whether a JWT-based generator is available. What is its plugin id?
evals.expected_output: The preview_url_generator plugin manager has a definition with id 'jwt' (label 'JSON Web Tokens'), provided by next_jwt. Discoverable via \Drupal::service('plugin.manager.next.preview_url_generator')->getDefinitions().

evals.prompt: This site has been configured to use JWT-based preview URLs for Next.js. Inspect the live next.settings configuration and state which preview URL generator is currently active.
evals.expected_output: next.settings.preview_url_generator is 'jwt', so the active generator (\Drupal::service('next.settings.manager')->getPreviewUrlGenerator()->getId()) is jwt.

evals.prompt: I want my Next.js preview links to use JSON Web Tokens (per-user access) instead of the default OAuth-based ones. Switch the next module's preview URL generator to next_jwt's JWT generator and save it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: next.settings.preview_url_generator is set to 'jwt' (e.g. drush cset next.settings preview_url_generator jwt), so the active preview URL generator is the JWT plugin.

evals.prompt: Configure the next module to generate preview URLs with next_jwt's JWT generator AND set its secret_expiration to 60 (minutes). Apply both changes to the live next.settings.
evals.expected_output: next.settings.preview_url_generator = 'jwt' and next.settings.preview_url_generator_configuration.secret_expiration = 60 (set both keys on the next.settings config object and save).
